transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Ramirez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Chen (Elm Product), Dev Kapoor (Elm CTO), Jordan Lee (Elm ML)

Summary:
Elm Ventures is evaluating Redwood for a fast time-to-first-token sprint: self-serve API with free credits to prototype, and then a decision point between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for production. Primary concerns: latency/cost tradeoffs, security/SOC two and KMS, and ability to run a quick benchmark on their sample payloads.

Topics:
- Quickstart and credits
- Time-to-first-token / dev experience
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision criteria
- Security/compliance (SOC 2, SSO, KMS)
- Performance expectations and benchmarking

Action items (recap at end) included above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Maria: yes good to go, thanks Alex.
[00:08] Dev: yep loud and clear.
[00:12] Alex: quick intro, i'm Alex on AE at Redwood, with Samir our solutions engineer. we work with teams to get to first token quickly, then help decide hosted versus dedicated or private based on your needs.
[00:28] Samir: hey all, i'll be the technical lead on this calls, happy to dig into perf and infra.
[00:34] Maria: awesome. high level we want to spin up a small prototype in a week — product needs to demo LLM chat to stakeholders. primary question is time-to-first-token and also what we should plan for after prototype (hosted or dedicated).
[00:48] Alex: great, that's exactly our typical flow. we give free credits, a quickstart with SDKs, and usually it takes teams a few hours to a day to hit first token if they have a simple prompt path.
[00:59] Jordan: curious — what's in the quickstart? is there a docker image or is it pure API?
[01:06] Samir: mostly API + SDKs, we also have a small sample repo with a dockerized example for local dev. you can run straight against the hosted API or point to a private endpoint if you go that route later.
[01:18] Dev: and the creds — how do we get them? do you hand out long lived keys?
[01:22] Alex: we issue short-term free credits through the console and you can create API keys. for production you rotate and integrate with your secrets manager; if you use Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM.
[01:34] Maria: security question — we need SOC two audit docs, SSO with SAML and role-based access. do you have those?
[01:41] Alex: yes we have SOC 2 type 2, SSO via SAML/SCIM, and RBAC in the console. i'll share our security pack. apologies the transcript sometimes shows SOC two as SOC too, but yes it's SOC 2.
[01:58] Jordan: good. on perf — our target for production is sub-200ms for short responses and 20k tokens/day across a cluster; for the prototype it's more like 5-10 qps. how do you recommend we start?
[02:12] Samir: for the proto, hosted API with free credits is fastest. for the numbers you mentioned, Dedicated is common to get predictable throughput. Private (VPC/on-prem) is chosen when data residency or strict network controls are required.
[02:27] Dev: can you be more specific on cost and latency differences? e.g. hosted vs dedicated quantization options?
[02:34] Samir: sure, hosted uses our shared pools with optimized kernels; latency can be slightly variable but usually very tight. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, consistent latencies and better throughput per dollar at scale. quantization benefits depend on model; we support int8/4 paths which reduce cost. i can run numbers on your workload.
[02:53] Maria: are there model restrictions on hosted? we need certain open models and we'd like to test a fine-tuned variant eventually.
[03:00] Alex: hosted has a catalog of vetted models, and you can bring your own model to Dedicated or Private. we also support model pinning and rollout policies so fine-tuning workflows are compatible.
[03:12] Jordan: how about prefix caching or KV cache? our chat uses long histories for context windows — can that be cached?
[03:19] Samir: yes we have KV/prefix caching in the runtime. some transcripts show 'K-V cache' or 'K V cache' — the tech is consistent. caching dramatically reduces per-token compute for repeated prefixes.
[03:33] Dev: ok. onbenchmarks — what do you need from us to run a realistic bench?
[03:38] Samir: sample payload distribution (payload sizes, typical prompt lengths, tokens per reply), concurrency targets, and any latency SLOs. if you share a small dataset we can run an estimate and a rough bench on hosted or our dedicated perf cluster.
[03:52] Maria: timeline wise we need something by next Friday to demo to investors. is that feasible?
[03:57] Alex: feasible. we can get you credits and a quickstart today, and Samir can run a quick perf estimate once Jordan sends the payloads. then we can book a bench next week.
[04:10] Jordan: question — do you support streaming and function calling? we have tool integrations for retrieval.
[04:15] Samir: yes streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. streaming is available on hosted and dedicated. streaming behaviour may differ slightly depending on model and payload.
[04:27] Dev: any gotchas with rate limits during early testing?
[04:30] Alex: default free-tier rate limits are conservative but we can temporarily bump them for a pilot. for production we advise committed Dedicated capacity if sustained RPS is needed.
[04:42] Maria: on the costing — can you show example unit economics? like tokens/$ for typical chat flows?
[04:49] Samir: i will prepare a cost sheet based on your sample prompts. quick note: batching and caching are the two biggest levers to reduce tokens/$ by reducing compute time per token.
[05:03] Jordan: for the sample prompt i mentioned, most requests are 512 token prompts and ~350 token outputs. that's heavier than a standard single-turn chat.
[05:12] Samir: got it. that will affect latency and cost; i'll run a scenario with that distribution.
[05:18] Maria: regarding compliance/regulatory: we operate in healthcare-adjacent workflows, so audit trails and data retention policies are important. do you have fine-grained logs and retention configs?
[05:28] Alex: yes audit logs, per-request tracing, and configurable retention. with Private you can keep logs in your VPC and meet stricter retention rules.
[05:39] Dev: if we wanted Private, how long does onboarding take?
[05:42] Alex: Private on-prem deployments vary but idearly 4-8 weeks depending on the integration depth. VPC-hosted private control plane can be faster, often a few weeks. Dedicated is quickest for production-like guarantees if you don't need full on-prem.
[05:58] Jordan: what's the path to bring our own model? do you support conversion?
[06:03] Samir: we support standard formats; sometimes we run a light conversion/quantization step and validate performance. it depends on the model architecture. we'll help with that during onboarding.
[06:13] Maria: are there enterprise contracts required for Dedicated? or is it self-serve?
[06:18] Alex: Dedicated typically involves a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual) and optional SLA. for smaller pilots you can start with hosted and then convert to Dedicated.
[06:29] Dev: any examples of customers that started on hosted then moved to Dedicated?
[06:33] Alex: yes several — we often see PLG teams prototype on hosted then commit to Dedicated as usage grows. i can share anonymized case studies.
[06:44] Jordan: competitor question — how different is your latency vs Anthropic or OpenAI for similar models?
[06:50] Samir: it's model-dependent; we optimize kernels and batching aggressively so in many cases our hosted latency is competitive. for tight SLOs Dedicated is better to avoid noisy neighbors.
[07:03] Maria: chat is going well — can you walk us through what the quickstart steps will look like?
[07:07] Alex: sure: 1) create account and claim free credits, 2) follow the quickstart repo (node/python), 3) integrate an API key and run sample chat, 4) share sample payloads for perf estimate, 5) optionally schedule a bench. we'll include monitoring/tracing examples.
[07:25] Jordan: is there a sample billing dashboard to show token spend per route?
[07:29] Samir: yes the Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and traces. helpful for optimizing prompts and routes.
[07:38] Dev: for restricted data we may need to ensure model outputs are not stored; is that configurable?
[07:44] Alex: yes you can opt-out of data retention on hosted for certain contracts, and with Private you control all storage. we'll share the policy doc.
[07:54] Maria: what's the recommended approach for our investor demo? quickstart hosted for speed, yes?
[07:59] Alex: yes, hosted with credits for the demo. if you need steady low-latency we can temporarily provision Dedicated test capacity for the bench.
[08:11] Jordan: how quickly can we get Dedicated test capacity?
[08:15] Samir: we can often spin a short-lived dedicated pool for a bench within a week depending on scheduling; i'll confirm availability when we book.
[08:24] Maria: ok — next steps recap?
[08:27] Alex: i'll email the quickstart, credits, security pack, and pricing comparison by tomorrow. Samir will schedule the bench once you provide payloads. Jordan/Dev to send prompt distribution.
[08:39] Maria: perfect.
[08:41] Dev: thanks everyone.
[08:44] --- mid-call technical dive ---
[09:00] Samir: Jordan, can you share typical concurrency spikes? are they bursty or steady?
[09:08] Jordan: mostly bursty, spikes around demo opens and nightly summary jobs. average overnight queue is low, day peaks to 150-200 requests in short windows.
[09:20] Samir: ok for bursty patterns we recommend autoscaling dedicated pools with burst capacity or routing policies that fall back to hosted if capacity is exhausted.
[09:31] Dev: fallback — would responses degrade or would you route to a smaller model?
[09:35] Samir: we do automated fallback to compatible model variants or regions. responses may vary but system keeps you online.
[09:45] Jordan: and tracing — can we correlate an application request id to Redwood traces?
[09:49] Samir: yes pass a request-id header and it surfaces in the trace. we also export traces to common tracing backends.
[09:58] Maria: anything else we should be aware of when prototyping to avoid surprises when scaling?
[10:03] Samir: watch token growth (small prompt changes can balloon tokens), enable caching for repeated prefixes, and plan for batching thresholds. also consider quantization compatibility if you migrate.
[10:18] Dev: on quantization — does it change output quality much?
[10:21] Samir: at int8/4 there can be small quality shifts; we recommend a regression check with your eval prompts. Redwood Optimize can run quantization recommendations.
[10:35] Jordan: i'll want to run a quick eval harness to catch regressions before switching modes.
[10:39] Samir: perfect, we can help set that up.
[10:44] --- near end of call recap ---
[11:00] Alex: recap: we'll send quickstart + credits + security docs, Samir will run perf estimate and book bench pending payloads, Elm to send prompts and concurrency patterns.
[11:14] Maria: thanks — please include contact for enterprise/contract questions because we may need a procurement timeline.
[11:19] Alex: noted, i'll include that and a sample procurement checklist.
[11:24] Dev: thanks everyone.
[11:26] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up.

(Transcript ends — calls often have small transcription errors; names sometimes appear as 'Sam' instead of 'Samir', 'SOC two' etc.)
